results.title: Ghanaian researchers use AI to develop more efficient, affordable solar panels
results.content: Ghanaian researchers are using artificial intelligence (AI) to identify materials that could make solar panels more efficient, affordable, and environmentally friendly, potentially expanding access to renewable energy. The research, supported by the French Embassy in Ghana, uses AI-powered computational methods to identify suitable material combinations for photovoltaic cells, which convert sunlight into electricity. Researchers hope to increase solar-cell conversion efficiency from the current level of about 22% to between 25% and 30%, while building local capacity to develop solar technologies.

results.title: Police explain why only one Obuasi SHTS abuse complaint has been investigated
results.content: The police have defended their handling of sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, amid questions over why investigations have so far focused on one complaint despite at least 19 girls reportedly alleging abuse. Bekwai Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Lloyd Baidoo, said the police investigate complaints brought to their attention and could pursue additional allegations if other victims reported them or relevant information was formally submitted. Speaking on JoyNews’ Top Story on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, he rejected suggestions that the police were not responding adequately to the growing public concern over the case.

results.title: Yaw Nsarkoh questions judiciary’s use of contempt powers, calls for independent prosecutor
results.content: Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has questioned the judiciary’s use of contempt powers, arguing that the authority should not be used to discourage legitimate scrutiny of judicial decisions. Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Mr Nsarkoh said judicial authority, like any other form of power, must be subject to critical examination and accountability. “If judges sit in court, and this happened, I'm not making it up, it's not AI, if judges sit in court and write into judgment that we have freedom of speech, but not freedom after speech, why on God's earth should we be unsure whether such wanton abuse of power can be described as professionally irresponsible?” he asked.

results.title: Yaw Nsarkoh questions relevance of palanquin tradition, calls for cultural rethinking
results.content: Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has questioned the continued practice of carrying chiefs in palanquins, challenging Ghanaians to examine whether every cultural tradition remains beneficial in a changing society. Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Mr Nsarkoh said the practice illustrated the need to question long-standing customs and consider when modifications become necessary for progressive innovation. He recounted watching a video of a chief dancing in a palanquin carried by young men, questioning whether the practice should automatically be defended as culture.
